questions.q: Why is the ML lifecycle described as a loop rather than a straight line?
options: Because monitoring a deployed model shows when data has changed, sending you back to prepare data and retrain
Because training always has to be repeated three times
Because deployment always fails the first time
Because notebooks must be rerun from the top before each release
questions.explain: Data keeps changing after deployment, so monitoring feeds back into data preparation and retraining.

questions.q: What does MLOps add on top of ordinary DevOps?
options: Nothing; it is just a new name for DevOps
Versioning and management of data and models, which change independently of code
A requirement to use notebooks in production
Replacing automated tests with manual review
questions.explain: An ML system changes when its data or model changes, not only its code, so those artifacts must be versioned and traceable too.

questions.q: In Google Cloud's maturity levels, what characterizes level 1?
options: Every step is performed manually in a notebook
Fully automated CI/CD for the pipeline code itself, with no data validation needed
An automated training pipeline that can be rerun on fresh data
A model is deployed once and never retrained
questions.explain: Level 0 is manual, level 1 automates the ML training pipeline, and level 2 adds CI/CD for the pipeline itself.

questions.q: In the lesson's lifecycle.py, what is the purpose of the check `metrics["accuracy"] >= 0.75` before joblib.dump?
options: It is a validation gate: the model is saved only if it clears a threshold
It speeds up training
It converts accuracy into a probability
It splits the data into train and test sets
questions.explain: The gate prevents a poor model from being saved. The 0.75 value is illustrative; Chapter 4 covers real automated validation.

questions.q: Why does the lesson fix random seeds such as random_state=0 in the script?
options: Because scikit-learn refuses to run without a seed
To make the model more accurate
To keep the saved file small
So a rerun produces identical splits and results, making runs repeatable and comparable
questions.explain: Fixed seeds make the workflow deterministic, so running it twice gave the identical accuracy of 0.768.
